$comment: Numeric bounds the native renderer enforces on read, declared once so the Editor can enforce the
same ones on write. Without this the scene stores a value the renderer refuses: typing 500 into a
spot light's cone angle saved 500, showed 500 and drew 179 — three numbers for one property.
Rust side: services/render-daemon/tests/renderer_clamps.rs feeds out-of-range values through
prepare_scene and asserts the prepared light matches the bounds below. It asserts behaviour rather
than re-reading a constant, so a clamp that moves in the renderer fails the test.
Only the properties the *native* renderer clamps belong here. Camera and slab bounds are enforced by
the browser Preview alone today (the native renderer does not prepare cameras at all), so they live
in the TypeScript table with their source cited and are not claimed as cross-language.
